The goal is minimum cost, or -1 if no assignment is possible.","source_ids":["task"]},{"statement":"Fixed parentheses cost zero. The length is 1 to 200000, and each cost is an integer from 0 to 1000000000.","source_ids":["task"]},{"statement":"The required output is one integer. Both supplied public examples have output -1.","source_ids":["task","public1","public2"]}],"open_requirements":["Develop and justify an algorithm that meets the input limits and handles impossible assignments.","Determine implementation details, including cost accumulation and input parsing; no programming language is specified."],"tentative_options":[{"id":"greedy_heap","method":"Hypothetically start each '?' as ')', track prefix balance, and use a priority queue of incremental costs for changing earlier '?' to '(' when needed to repair a deficit; check the final balance.","unverified_assumptions":["This greedy choice yields a minimum-cost assignment satisfying all prefixes and the final equal-count condition.","The final-balance check is sufficient to identify infeasibility after the prefix repairs."]},{"id":"constrained_selection","method":"Hypothetically formulate the choices of which '?' become '(' as a minimum-cost selection problem with prefix lower bounds and a final required count.","unverified_assumptions":["The formulation admits an algorithm efficient enough for length 200000.","Its cost and constraint representation handles all fixed-parenthesis positions correctly."]}],"possible_checks":["Test any proposed method against both supplied examples.","For short strings, exhaustively enumerate '?' assignments and compare feasibility and minimum cost with the proposed algorithm.","Verify correctness at prefixes and at the final total, and check that the chosen integer type safely holds accumulated costs."]}
